CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sharon Brooks is a 48-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain that began four days ago while skiing. Patient reports she was attempting moguls when her ski strap became caught on her finger, causing it to hyperextend or bend backward. She has tried ice and ibuprofen for pain management, but symptoms persist. Pain is exacerbated by movement.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies pain with palpation over the proximal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Reports pain with flexion of the finger. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Constipation (recent)
Appendectomy at age 18

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for constipation
Ibuprofen (as needed for pain)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is an active skier.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right hand index finger exam reveals tenderness over the distal phalanx. Tenderness present over the distal interphalangeal joint. No tenderness over the proximal interphalangeal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Finger flexion possible with pain. Finger extension possible. Patient able to touch thumb with index finger. Full range of motion achieved.

RESULTS
X-ray of right index finger: Normal with no fractures. All structures align appropriately.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right index finger contusion on the tip of the finger with no fracture.
1. Aluminum foam splint to right index finger
2. Motrin 600 mg every six hours for approximately one week
3. Patient to call and return for follow-up if symptoms do not improve
